scenes.narration: This is guardrails-lens, the last review pass in the writing loop. Tessl review run scores it in the terminal: validation checks first, then judges for the content and the description. It comes back at ninety percent. The description judge says why. There are no phrases a person would actually use to ask for it, and some overlap with general editing skills.

Tessl review fix acts on that feedback. It rewrites the skill, reviews the rewrite, and keeps going until it reaches the target score. Each round takes a few minutes, so this part is sped up. The skill reached ninety-five percent, and only the description changed. It now leads with the argument problems this lens catches, and adds the phrases people use to ask for it.
A fresh review confirms it: ninety-five percent.

Now the change goes through the same gate as any other. Push the branch, open the pull request, and watch the checks. A Tessl skill review runs on every pull request that touches a skill, next to the plugin validation.

On GitHub, the review lands as a single comment on the pull request: a score for each changed skill, any validation warnings, and the full breakdown from each judge one click away. Nothing was published to the registry. It all ran in the repository's own workflow.
